chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

about a man who bound up his hair while he was performing tamattuʿ, then came to Makkah, completed his rites, untied the braids of his head, trimmed, applied oil, and deemed himself released from ihram.
He عليه السلام said: “He must offer the blood-sacrifice of a sheep.”

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: entered the state of being released from ihram
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: the sacrifice of a sheep as expiation
key_terms.عِقَاصَ: the braids or tied locks of hair

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a mutamattiʿ who tied his hair and then trimmed and exited ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person performing Hajj al-tamattuʿ who had bound his hair and then proceeded with trimming and release from ihram. The Imam عليه السلام rules that such a person owes the sacrifice of a sheep as expiation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2744 - Abdullah ibn Sinan asked Abu Abdullah (as)
about a man performing tamattu‘ who tied up his hair before arriving in Mecca. He completed his rites, untied his hair, trimmed it, applied oil, and considered himself released from ihram.
Imam (as) said: "He must offer a sheep as expiation."
